cues.zh: 但你知道吗，哪怕在 24 小时后能激发一点自噬，我都会非常非常高兴。但如果我想把自噬最大化，我就会选择断食三天。那我来解释一下什么是自噬。关于自噬，两年前的诺贝尔奖得主就是因为研究自噬而获奖的。自噬过程中发生的是，当你像这样缺乏营养时，身体会感知到没有营养摄入。体内有一种叫做 mTOR 的东西。

cues.en: mTOR levels go really really low. This is a protein kinase in the body and it goes really really low and that turns on autophagy. What turns off autophagy is mTOR levels are high. What causes mTOR levels to go high is eating mostly proteins. So let's come back again to autophagy. So what autophagy does is that it takes your cells and the cell
cues.zh: mTOR 水平会变得非常非常低。这是体内的一种蛋白激酶，它的水平降得很低很低，就会开启自噬。而阻断自噬的是过高的 mTOR 水平。导致 mTOR 水平升高的主要是进食蛋白质。所以我们再回到自噬。自噬所做的是，它会作用于你的细胞，而细胞……

cues.en: has a lipoprotein membrane around it, and there's all the intracellular organelles in it. But in the course of time, those cells, the intracellular organelles, some of them become redundant. There's protein lying around. Whenever there's work, there's going to be garbage. So there are old intracellular organelles and some proteinaceous materials that are just lying around in the cytoplasm. So the body says, I need energy. Recycle. I need to recycle.
cues.zh: 周围包裹着一层脂蛋白膜，里面有各种细胞内细胞器。但随着时间的推移，这些细胞和胞内细胞器中，有一部分会变得多余。周围散落着闲置的蛋白质。只要有代谢工作，就会产生垃圾。因此会有老旧的胞内细胞器和一些蛋白质残留物闲置在细胞质里。于是身体就会说：“我需要能量，回收利用，我需要回收这些废物。”

cues.en: So the first thing it does, the cell stays alive, and it takes those intracellular organelles, breaks them down, packages them into the lysosome, and digests it, breaks it down into its pieces, so whether it's the sarcoplasmic reticulum or other intracellular organelles, breaks them all down and exports it out of the cell. Once it's exported from the cell into the bloodstream, the bloodstream says, aha!
cues.zh: 所以它首先做的是让细胞保持存活；它把这些细胞内细胞器取出来，分解，打包进溶酶体，消化，把它们拆成碎片。所以不管是肌浆网还是其他细胞内细胞器，都会全部分解，再输出到细胞外。一旦从细胞输出到血液中，血液就会说：啊哈！

cues.en: I've got some new building blocks now, and the body re-utilizes that. Okay, so the body now starts utilizing your intracellular organelles. So you're recycling your cells. So your cell doesn't die. It goes into a state of recycling. And you recycle your mitochondria as well, so mitochondrial parts, because there's a lot of oxidative stress going on in the mitochondria. So what happens is that it
cues.zh: 我现在有了一些新的构建块，身体会重新利用它们。好，所以身体现在开始利用你细胞内的细胞器。也就是说，你在回收自己的细胞。细胞不会死，而是进入一种回收状态。线粒体也会被回收，线粒体的各个部分也会，因为线粒体里发生着大量氧化应激。所以接下来发生的是，它——

cues.en: That cell is now going to be depleted of its old, non-functional parts. And then when you do it, guess what? It gets repaired first. All those organelles. So you basically rejuvenate your cells. Now, if you're constantly eating, you will not rejuvenate those cells. And the biochemistry is so beautiful that these cells now are functioning better, they're younger, and...
cues.zh: 那个细胞现在会耗尽其旧的、失去功能的部件。然后你这样做时，猜怎么着？它先得到修复。所有那些细胞器。所以你基本上是在让细胞恢复年轻。现在，如果你不停地吃东西，就不会让这些细胞恢复年轻。而生物化学的美妙之处在于，这些细胞现在功能更好、更年轻，而且……

cues.en: they are going to last longer, they're more resilient also to disease. I'll come to that in a minute. So autophagy makes your cells better, younger, restoration. It's like a reset switch. So how do those organelles redo themselves? Well, they rebuild themselves because when you then eat, because you've had autophagy, a signal goes from those cells to the bone marrow to say, hey, listen, I used up my intracellular organelles.
cues.zh: 它们会更持久，对疾病也更有韧性。我稍后会讲到这一点。所以自噬让你的细胞更好、更年轻，得到修复。它就像一个重置开关。那么这些细胞器如何重建自己呢？它们会重建，因为当你随后进食时，由于你已经发生过自噬，那些细胞会向骨髓发出信号说：嘿，听着，我用完了我的细胞内细胞器。

cues.en: When you get new ones, new supplies, send them to me. So the bone marrow, when you eat, makes stem cells. Have you heard of stem cells? No, it'll cost you a million dollars. Just go out and get some. It'll cost you a whole lot of money and it won't work. Because when you inject stem cells from the outside, the residence rates are wrong because they didn't get the message.
cues.zh: 等你拿到新的、新的补给时，把它们送给我。所以骨髓在你吃东西时会制造干细胞。你听说过干细胞吗？没听过？那得花你一百万美元。直接出去弄点吧。会花你一大笔钱，而且还没用。因为从外部注射干细胞时，驻留率会不对，因为它们没收到信息。

cues.en: of where to go to. It's all artificial. So it doesn't know. So the brain, look, I injected stem cells in the heart. When patients are myocardial infarctions, I was here doing the study upstairs. And what was the recidence rate? Recidence rate is how many of the stem cells actually ended up in the muscle where I wanted it to stay and repair the heart. Less than 0.1%. Did the ejection fractions go up? No change in ejection fraction.
cues.zh: 该往哪里去的信息。这全是人为的，所以它不知道。于是，大脑——你看，我把干细胞注射到心脏里。当患者发生心肌梗死时，我当时就在楼上做这项研究。那驻留率是多少？驻留率是指有多少干细胞真正到达了我希望它停留并修复心脏的肌肉里。不到0.1%。射血分数上升了吗？射血分数没有变化。

cues.en: So injecting stem cells from the outside does nothing for you. It was good to study stem cells and it still is for the reason that you need to harness nature's way of giving you stem cells. Do you want a stem cell transplant right now? You're going to fast. It's the fastest way to increase your stem cells. So these stem cells come out of the bone marrow. It's called refeeding reward. And they go into the organs and replenish cells that have died.
cues.zh: 所以从外部注射干细胞对你没什么用。研究干细胞过去有价值，现在仍然有价值，因为你需要利用大自然给你干细胞的方式。你想现在就做干细胞移植吗？你要去禁食。这是增加干细胞最快的方法。这些干细胞从骨髓里出来。这叫做再进食奖励。它们进入器官，补充已经死亡的细胞。

cues.en: and change the machinery in those cells as well. So there's a whole rejuvenation process. You are a younger, better, more resilient person than you were before. And this has all been documented over and over again. But there's no industry that's going to support me because there's no financial gain if you get better and younger and live longer. Because there's no one there to make money out of. No one makes money when you're fast. They lose money.
cues.zh: 同时改变这些细胞内部的机制。所以这是一个彻底的焕新过程。你会变得比以前更年轻、更健康、更有韧性。这一切都已被反复证实。但没有任何产业会支持我，因为如果你变得更健康、更年轻、更长寿，他们是赚不到钱的。因为根本没法从你身上捞到钱。当你断食时，没人能赚钱，他们只会亏钱。

cues.en: So boost your growth hormone, boost your stem cells. This has been very well documented. Not only in humans, in animals too. Well documented, over and over again. It's just that nobody's ever heard of it. Anyone thinks, oh, fasting is just fasting. It's starvation. It's no good. But there's so much science behind this. So the next benefit, of course, is stem cell mobilization that occurs. And to get the maximum benefit of that,
cues.zh: 所以它能提升你的生长激素，激活你的干细胞。这已经得到了充分的证实。不仅在人体中，在动物身上也是如此。证据确凿，反复得到验证。只是从未有人听说过罢了。大家总觉得，哎呀，断食不就是挨饿吗，那是饥荒，对身体不好。但这背后蕴藏着大量的科学依据。当然，下一个好处就是干细胞的动员。而要想获得最大的益处，

cues.en: You can't just do overnight fast. No, you really need to fast. Because for the bone marrow to say, I'm going to come in and replace, you've got to really have reached that point of replacement. So you can't speed it up either. So the question is, can I do a three day fast? Of course I can do a three day fast. You've got to prepare yourself mentally. You've got to prepare yourself physically for the environment. Make sure that, you know,
cues.zh: 只做隔夜断食是不行的。不，你必须真正去断食。因为要让骨髓开始说“我要进来替换更新了”，你必须真正达到那个更新的临界点。所以这个过程你也急不得。那么问题来了，我能做三天断食吗？当然可以。你必须在心理上做好准备。你必须在身体和环境上做好准备。确保，你知道的，

cues.en: You're with your best friends and environment. And you've got to have water so that you don't get dehydrated. So you can do it. All of us can do it. So you can fast for different reasons. So when would I want autophagy? I would want autophagy one, just to live longer. Number two, let me tell you something. If you do a seven-day water fast, the studies done in Boston at the university showed
cues.zh: 你处在最好的朋友和环境陪伴中。而且你必须补充水分，以免脱水。所以你是可以做到的，我们所有人都能做到。因此出于不同的目的，你可以进行断食。那么我什么时候会需要自噬呢？我需要自噬，第一是为了更长寿。第二，让我告诉你一件事。如果你进行七天的纯水断食，波士顿某大学的研究表明，

cues.en: that your lifetime probability of getting cancer is reduced by more than 70%. Some studies even higher. Because the cells that are going to die off in the state of the fast are going to be your cancer cells. Because your cancer cells, look, if I want to do a PET scan on you, I'm going to give you radioactive materials of glucose in it.
cues.zh: 你一生中患癌症的概率会降低70%以上。有些研究甚至显示得更高。因为在断食状态下死去的细胞，往往就是那些癌细胞。因为对于癌细胞，你看，如果我要给你做 PET 扫描，我会给你注射含有葡萄糖的放射性物质。

cues.en: excuse me, the glucose is really low, and the insulin level is really low, so the nutrients that the cancer cells want are not there, cancer cells do die off. So, let's talk about cancer for a second. So the studies have been done, and if you fast a person only for 36 hours, that's it, and then give them chemotherapy in that state, they're going to tolerate the chemotherapy better, they're going to have less side effects from the chemotherapy, it's going to be
cues.zh: 抱歉，此时血糖极低，胰岛素水平也极低，所以癌细胞渴望的营养物质根本不存在，癌细胞确实会死掉。那么，我们再来聊一下癌症。研究表明，如果让一个人仅断食36小时，就这么久，然后在这个状态下给他们进行化疗，他们对化疗的耐受度会更好，化疗带来的副作用也会更少，这将会促成

cues.en: death of cancer cells and your normal cells are more resilient now. And you're going to get less death of your normal cells. Do you understand what I'm saying? So what happens when you're fasting, your normal cells become more resilient. So when you give the chemo, only the weak guys die, which is the cancer cells. Because you've strengthened through this fasting process your normal cells.
cues.zh: 癌细胞的死亡，而你的正常细胞现在变得更有韧性了。你的正常细胞死亡量会大大减少。你明白我的意思吗？也就是说，在断食时，你的正常细胞变得更顽强了。所以当你进行化疗时，死掉的只有那些脆弱的家伙，也就是癌细胞。因为通过这个断食过程，你已经强化了自身的正常细胞。

cues.en: So I wanted to do this protocol upstairs in the bone marrow unit, where we do a lot of chemotherapy on these patients. But no, nobody said, okay, we want to do this project. They said it would be inhumane to tell our patients to fast before we give them chemotherapy. So what we do, we feed them, then they ad nauseate it, then they vomit, so we give them Zofran, and then they still don't do that, so then we'll put TPN on them.
cues.zh: 我本来想在楼上的骨髓科推行这个方案，我们给这些病人做很多化疗。但不行，没人说“好，我们想做这个项目”。他们说，让病人在化疗前禁食是不人道的。所以我们怎么做呢？先喂他们，然后他们恶心，接着吐，我们就给 Zofran；可他们还是吐，于是再上 TPN。

cues.en: Because we've all been indoctrinated that we have to feed, feed, feed, feed, feed. I'm just telling you all right now, if any of you get on my carnal infarction, you get admitted to the hospital, I'm making your NPO. I'll put IV fluids on you, I'll make your NPO. So even if you do vomit, you're not going to aspirate. You know how much aspiration we see in the hospital over here? Pneumonia and all that from aspiration is terrible. Because I'm force feeding you in a sense. Wait a second, your body is not hungry, don't eat. But no, if the trays get bored to you, you have to eat. You don't have to.
cues.zh: 因为我们都被灌输了必须喂、喂、喂、喂、喂。我现在就告诉你们，要是你们谁得了心肌梗死，住院了，我就让你禁食。我会给你上静脉输液，让你禁食。这样即使你吐了，也不会误吸。你知道我们这边医院见到多少误吸吗？误吸导致的肺炎之类的太糟糕了。因为从某种意义上说，我们是在强迫你吃。等等，你身体不饿，那就别吃。可不行，饭盘一端到你面前，你就得吃。其实你不必吃。

cues.en: There's a reason why you have anorexia when you're sick. Pay attention to your body. Your body's telling you don't eat, then don't eat, you won't die. You might die from eating. So, cancer. I predict that in the next five to ten years, there's going to be major cancer treatments associated with adjunctive fasting. And that's coming, definitely. It's on its way. What else can be useful? Autoimmune diseases.
cues.zh: 生病时没胃口是有原因的。注意你的身体。身体告诉你别吃，那就别吃，你不会死。你倒可能因为吃而死。再说癌症。我预测未来五到十年，会出现与辅助禁食相关的重大癌症疗法。这一定会来。已经在路上了。还有什么会有用？自身免疫病。

cues.en: There's numerous studies to say that you have inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, any of these conditions and you get a flare up of it, fast for three days. It's the most potent thing you can do as an anti-inflammatory. Because first and foremost, your bowels are totally quiet. There's no energy being used for digestion. Your body's energy resources will be utilized to repair yourself.
cues.zh: 大量研究表明，如果你有炎症性肠病、类风湿性关节炎、狼疮，或任何这类疾病，并且正在发作，就禁食三天。作为抗炎手段，这是你能做的最强效的事。因为首先，你的肠道完全安静下来。没有能量被用于消化。身体的能量资源会被用来修复自身。

cues.en: A lot of autoimmune diseases start from your gut as well. It gives your gut a chance to heal so that you get less leaky gut syndrome. So that that fast actually heals, it gives your gut a chance to heal as well. Autoimmune diseases get better. And what about diabetes? Diabetes definitely gets better because I just told you the insulin resistance gets better. So that gets better. What about Alzheimer's? Oh yeah, you know, poor granny, we can't pull the tray away from her.
cues.zh: 很多自身免疫病也从肠道开始。它让肠道有机会修复，从而减少肠漏综合征。所以这种禁食确实能修复，也让肠道有机会修复。自身免疫病会好转。那糖尿病呢？糖尿病肯定会好转，因为我刚说了胰岛素抵抗会改善。所以它也会好转。阿尔茨海默病呢？哦对，你知道，可怜的奶奶，我们总不能把饭盘从她面前拿走吧。

cues.en: But sometimes it's the best thing you could actually do. Give her lots of liquids and don't feed Granny for three days if she's got dementia. Social services will be after you. It could be anybody, not just the Granny. But don't feed her for three days. Just give her lots of water. I promise you, neurologically, she'll start waking up. The fog will go away. The confusion will get better. It can get better. And it should get better.
cues.zh: 但有时候，这恰恰是你最该做的事。如果奶奶有痴呆，就给她大量液体，三天别喂她。社会服务部门会找上门来。可能是任何人，不只是奶奶。但三天别喂她。只给她大量水。我保证，从神经功能上看，她会开始清醒过来。脑雾会散去。迷糊会好转。它能好转。而且应该好转。

cues.en: And there's no humming trying because she won't die in three days. So three-day water fast. So what do I mean by the water fast? Three-day water fast. That means you can only drink water for three days. So drink lots of water. Now, why do you need to drink so much water? Because all reactions occur in water. And secondly, you pee a lot when you're fasting. I'm not drinking that much. I'm not eating it. How come I'm peeing so much? It's because when your insulin levels go down, insulin holds onto water. Now there's no more insulin. So that water gets diarrhea start of your body.
cues.zh: 没什么好犹豫的，因为三天饿不死人。所以做三天清水断食。那我说的清水断食是什么意思呢？三天清水断食。意思是这三天你只能喝水。所以要多喝水。那为什么需要喝这么多水呢？因为体内的所有反应都是在水中进行的。其次，断食期间你的尿量会很多。“我又没喝那么多，也没吃东西，怎么尿这么多？”这是因为当你的胰岛素水平下降时——原本胰岛素是会锁住水分的。现在没有胰岛素了，那些水分就会像腹泻一样排出体外。

cues.en: So you will notice that you pee a lot, so you need to drink more when you're fasting. That's number one. Now what about electrolytes? Well, electrolytes will be conserved by your kidneys. Your kidneys are very good at holding on to electrolytes. So there's plenty of electrolytes in the body. Do you know that if I have sodium, if I don't take in sodium, the last molecule of sodium will be reabsorbed by my kidneys. Not a single molecule will be in my urine. That's how good it is.
cues.zh: 所以你会发现自己频繁排尿，因此断食期间你需要补充更多水分。这是第一点。那电解质怎么办呢？其实肾脏会为你保存电解质。你的肾脏非常擅长锁住电解质。所以体内有足够的电解质。你知道吗，如果我不摄入钠，肾脏会把最后一个钠分子都重新吸收回来。尿液里连一个分子都不会有。它的功能就是这么强大。

cues.en: So the kidneys will take care of everything. The kidneys will not allow you to lose sodium or potassium. Now, if you're already starting out with a half-empty plate, yeah, you may get some depletion, but you can get that tested. And on refeeding, I'll give you some clues on how to improve that when you refeed yourself. But it's unusual to get electrolyte in balance. But if you do get it, take a pinch of salt in the water.
cues.zh: 所以肾脏会处理好一切。肾脏不会让你流失钠或钾。当然，如果你本身底子就不足、电解质偏低，那确实可能会有些匮乏，但你可以去做检测。而在复食阶段，关于如何改善这一点，我会给你一些复食的建议。但电解质失衡其实很少见。不过如果真的出现了，就在水里加一小撮盐。

cues.en: And you'll find that your cramps get better, and your dizziness gets better, and your headaches get better. So these are complaints that a lot of patients have that, oh, you know, I was fasting, but mind, after about 15 hours, I had a bad headache. I'm going to drink more water with a little bit of salt in it, and put Himalayan salt, because that also has some magnesium and other things in it. And you'll feel a lot better. Dizziness is usually due to low blood pressure, because your blood pressure comes down.
cues.zh: 你就会发现抽筋缓解了，头晕缓解了，头痛也好了。很多患者都会抱怨说：“哎呀，我在断食，可是大概15个小时后，我头痛得厉害。”多喝点加了一点盐的水，最好加喜马拉雅粉盐，因为里面还含有镁等微量元素。你就会感觉好很多。头晕通常是因为血压降低，因为你的血压降下来了。

cues.en: So you get dizzy when you're fasting, it's not because your sugar's down, it's because your blood pressure's lower. Drink water and cramps. Some patient gets cramps, put the salt again. And also in the evening, put yourself in a tub of Epsom salts. Or you can get some magnesium, and there's a liquid magnesium you can just put on your skin, you can spray it, and that'll give you magnesium. And that's what it's all about. So give yourself salt, some magnesium, you'll start feeling better.
cues.zh: 所以断食期间头晕，并不是因为低血糖，而是因为血压变低了。多喝水；要是抽筋——有些患者会抽筋——那就再加点盐。另外晚上可以泡个泻盐浴。或者补充点镁，有一种液体镁可以直接涂在皮肤上，喷一喷，就能给你补充镁元素。关键就在这里。所以补点盐、补点镁，你就会开始好受很多。

cues.en: Patients say that, oh, I get so hungry. Well, hunger comes and goes. There's a ghrelin increase and decrease according to the circadian cycle. So all you have to do is pay attention. cues.zh: 因为里面富含甘氨酸，还有磷酸盐以及大量的矿物质。这些对你大有裨益，甚至还有镁。所以它能帮你缓解一些不适。多了解一下骨头汤吧。而且别买现成的，要自己熬。顺便说一下，现在关于低碳饮食有很多食谱，早餐、午餐或晚餐你想做什么都查得到，骨头汤的做法也应有尽有。我最常用也最喜欢的一本书是 Jason Fung 的书。

cues.en: Jason Fung, F-U-N-G. He's a nephrologist up in Canada, and he sees all this really heavy-duty diabetics, and he does amazing work. But you see, he's learned all these tricks to make success. So the potassium can fall, magnesium can fall, and phosphate. So refeeding, just be careful, use bone broth during that time. I already mentioned all the side effects, which are okay, coffee, tea. I mentioned the tea.
cues.zh: Jason Fung，拼作 F-U-N-G。他是加拿大的一位肾病专家，接诊的都是病情非常严重的糖尿病患者，他的工作成果令人惊叹。你看，他掌握了所有这些成功的门道。断食时钾、镁和磷酸盐的水平都可能会下降。所以复食时一定要小心，那段时间可以喝骨头汤。我之前提到过所有的副作用，那些都还算可控，咖啡、茶都可以喝，我刚才提到了茶。

cues.en: And black teeth. Pardon? Medicines. Yes. When you're doing fasting, it depends which medicine. Now, if you're taking diabetes medications, and I'm telling you all, if you're taking diabetes medications, they will cause a drop in your sugar level, and it could be a dangerous drop in your sugar level. Especially insulin should not be taken. And glyburide, clippazide, those agents should not be taken.
cues.zh: 还有红茶。什么？药物？没错。断食的时候，这取决于你吃的是哪种药。如果你正在服用糖尿病药物——我在此提醒大家，如果你在吃糖尿病药，它们会导致血糖骤降，而且可能降到危险的水平。尤其是胰岛素，绝对不能用。还有格列本脲、格列吡嗪，这类降糖药都不该服用。

cues.en: But don't do that without your physician knowing. You've got to involve your physician. If you're a diabetic patient, your physician needs to know about it. If your physician doesn't want to know about it and doesn't approve of you doing fasting, maybe you need to find another one. You see, because, and look, it's not bad. I look, physicians are great, but we're taught to treat illness. Get sick and I'll know what to do with you. But you want to stay healthy? Heck, I don't know.
cues.zh: 但切记不要瞒着你的主治医生擅自停药。一定要让医生参与进来。如果你是糖尿病患者，你的医生必须知情。如果你的医生不想了解，也不同意你断食，也许你该考虑换个医生了。因为你看，这倒不是说他们不好，医生都很优秀，但我们受到的教育是治病。你生病了我才知道怎么对付它。但你想保持健康？天哪，这我还真不知道。

cues.en: That's the problem we have. So it's not that they don't want to help you. It's just that they don't know. They've never been there to handle that kind of situation. I'll tell you what I do with my patients, okay? I stop the insulin right there. No more insulin, and I stop glaburide or any other agent that drops blood sugar except for metformin. I keep them on metformin. And then I tell them to measure the blood sugars. And for three days or two days, they may have high blood sugar, but that's not going to hurt them.
cues.zh: 这就是我们面临的问题。所以并不是他们不想帮你，只是他们根本不懂。他们从来没接触过、也没处理过这种情况。我来告诉你们我是怎么对待病人的，好吗？我当场就会给他们停掉胰岛素。不再使用胰岛素，停用格列本脲或除二甲双胍以外的任何降糖药。我让他们继续吃二甲双胍。然后我让他们密切监测血糖。在两三天内，他们的血糖可能会偏高，但这并不会对身体造成伤害。

cues.en: That's not going to hurt them. So if you look at what hurts you the most, it's a high insulin level that hurts you more. If your glucose level is a little bit high, okay, that may glycate some of your proteins, but it's temporary. It's not going to hurt you in the long term, but insulin will hurt you. So that's what I've done. And for most of them, after they're fast, they feel a lot better, and they can come off insulin. They should be able to come off insulin. But you've got to, you know, the trouble with physicians and myself included.
cues.zh: 那并不会伤害他们。所以如果你看看究竟什么对你的伤害最大，其实是高胰岛素水平对你的伤害更大。如果你的血糖稍微偏高一点，好吧，那可能会让某些蛋白质发生糖化，但这只是暂时的。长期来看它不会伤害你，但胰岛素却会。所以我就是这么做的。对他们大多数人来说，断食之后感觉好多了，而且他们可以停用胰岛素。他们本就应该能停掉胰岛素。但你必须……要知道，医生们面临的问题，包括我自己在内。

cues.en: We're so busy that ideally I would like to see you going on a fast and then I'll see you today because we discussed it. I'd like to see you again in a couple of days, at least. Now, if I'm going to stop your incident, I might want you to take your blood sugar every day, every day, at least four times, and report to my office, call the office, tell the nurse, my sugar is doing this, that, that, and have a very close follow up on that. The trouble is that...
cues.zh: 我们太忙了，按理说我最希望看到的是你开始断食，我们今天讨论过，我今天见你一面，然后我希望至少隔两三天再见你一次。现在，如果我要停掉你的胰岛素，我可能会要求你每天、每天至少测四次血糖，并向我的诊所汇报，打电话给诊所，告诉护士我的血糖是这个情况、那个情况，并对此进行非常密切的随访。问题在于……

cues.en: Our system is so broken that most physicians can't do that. And if they try to do that, they'll go broke. Because there's no reimbursement for any of this stuff. It's really terrible. But that's what I'm saying. Find a physician that you can at least talk with frequently, go and see frequently if you want to come off diabetes medications. Now all the other medications, blood pressure medication, you should take everything else. But you measure your blood pressure.
cues.zh: 我们的体制已经支离破碎，大多数医生根本做不到这一点。如果他们真这么做，就会破产。因为这些服务根本拿不到医保报销。这真的很糟糕。但我还是那句话：如果你想停掉糖尿病药物，至少要找一个你能经常沟通、能经常去面诊的医生。至于其他所有药物，比如降压药，其他的你都该照常吃。但你要测自己的血压。

cues.en: You've got to take things into your own hands because nobody is going to do it except you. You must take control of your life. We have become a society where we go to the doctor and say, fix me. No, you've got to do it yourself. You must take your blood sugars every day, get your ketone sticks over there, get your blood pressure machine, start taking your blood pressures. If your blood pressure starts going below 100, you call the doctor, it's about blood pressure level or just need to be on vasotag. Oh no, stop the vasotag. Good, fine, done. And that's what happens actually.
cues.zh: 你必须掌握主动权，因为除了你之外没人会替你操心。你必须掌控自己的生活。我们现在的社会风气是，大家去看医生然后说：“把我治好吧。”不，你得靠自己。你必须每天测血糖，买好那些酮体试纸，备好血压计，开始每天测血压。如果你的血压开始低于100，你就给医生打电话：“我的血压是这个水平，还需要继续吃 Vasotec 吗？”“哦不用了，把 Vasotec 停掉。”很好，没问题，搞定。实际上事情就是这样解决的。

cues.en: So it's hard to predict who's going to drop the blood pressure and who's not. But generally speaking, you've got to be very vigilant. And you need to doubt that you can quickly approach or a walk-in clinic that you can walk into. That's why I have my walk-in clinic, right? People can walk in. And yeah, they might have to wait, but at least they're going to be seen. And if I'm tied up, at least my practitioners will take care of the patient. So your blood pressure will drop.
cues.zh: 所以很难预测谁的血压会降下来，谁的不会。但总的来说，你必须保持高度警惕。而且你需要一个能快速联系上的医生，或者一个能随时挂号就诊的免预约诊所。这就是为什么我开了自己的免预约诊所，对吧？大家直接走进来就行。没错，他们可能得排队等，但至少能看上病。就算我抽不开身，至少我的诊疗助理也会照看好病人。所以你的血压是会降下来的。

cues.en: because you become volume depleted or because of your physiology changing. Your physiology is changing, that's where your blood pressure is dropping. So yeah, you can come off, look, high blood pressure, sugar, high triglycerides, and low HDL are all part of metabolic syndrome. This makes metabolic syndrome better. Therefore, your blood pressure will come down, your sugar will come down, your triglycerides will come down, and your HDL will go up.
cues.zh: 是因为血容量减少，还是因为生理机能发生了改变？其实是你的生理机能变了，血压才会降下来。所以你看，高血压、高血糖、高甘油三酯和低高密度脂蛋白，都是代谢综合征的表现。这样做能改善代谢综合征。因此，你的血压会降下来，血糖会降下来，甘油三酯会降下来，而高密度脂蛋白则会升上去。

cues.en: I told you all before that the lipid abnormalities that you see, very few of them are primary lipid abnormalities. The rest are all reflections of your glucose metabolism that has gone haywire. So the most important things to look for on your lipid panel is not your LDL. It's your triglycerides and HDL and the ratio of HDL to triglycerides. If it's off, you have a sugar problem.
cues.zh: 我之前跟你们说过，那些血脂异常的情况，极少数是原发性的。其余全都是糖代谢紊乱的反映。所以看血脂指标时，最重要的不是低密度脂蛋白，而是甘油三酯和高密度脂蛋白，以及两者之间的比值。如果这个比值不对，就说明你的糖代谢有问题。

cues.en: Even though your sugar is good or your hemoglobin A1C is good, if your triglycerides are high and your HDL law and the ratio is greater than two, you probably have high insulin levels. And that needs to be determined and the treatment of high insulin levels today is faster. Changing your diet and doing it. Now, what do I do six months down the road? The patient comes to me and says, oh, I've lost all this weight. Look, I feel great now. I'm down on my medications. I'm hardly taking anything now.
cues.zh: 即便你的血糖正常，糖化血红蛋白也正常，但如果甘油三酯偏高、高密度脂蛋白偏低，且两者的比值大于二，那你很可能有高胰岛素血症。这需要测出来，而如今治疗高胰岛素水平见效更快的方法，就是改变饮食并坚持下去。那么六个月后我会怎么做呢？患者来找我说：“看，我减了这么多体重，现在感觉棒极了。药量减了，现在几乎不用吃药了。”

cues.en: I will repeat his insulin levels. If they are good, I'll say, you know what? Things are much better now. You don't have to be so crazy about your diet anymore. But automatically, most of them still do time restricted feeding. Because they love it. They feel so good doing it. So very few go back to eating five times a day. So very important that we do this. I wanted to mention something else too. Yes?
cues.zh: 我会再测一次他的胰岛素水平。如果指标正常，我就会说：“你知道吗？情况已经好多了。饮食上不用再卡得那么严了。”但大多数人还是会自觉坚持限时进食。因为他们乐在其中，感觉非常棒。所以很少有人会倒退回一天吃五顿。因此坚持这样做非常重要。另外我还想提一件事。请讲？

cues.en: So the, you know, studies are very hard in humans, but I wanted to show you one study that was done in monkeys about fasting. So they took the monkeys, the rhesus monkeys, which we very closely related to them. They deserve more respect, I think. Rhesus monkeys. So they took the experimental group, gave them 30% less calories. The standard teaching for weight loss, 30% less calories, right? So 30% less calories.
cues.zh: 大家知道，针对人类的研究很难做，但我想给大家看一项关于猴子断食的研究。研究人员选了猕猴，它们和人类亲缘关系很近。我觉得猕猴值得我们更多的尊重。研究人员把实验组的热量摄入减少了30%。这就是标准的减重法则，热量少30%，对吧？就是少摄入30%的热量。

cues.en: And the control group, they gave them milk protein, corn oil, sugar, and unlimited feeding times. Pretty much like an American diet. That was the control group. And then what they did is they looked at the outcome at five years in these disease monkeys. There was 20, those who had restricted calories, the 30% restricted calories, they lived 26% more than the control group.
cues.zh: 而对照组吃的是乳蛋白、玉米油和糖，并且不限进食时间。这基本就跟美式饮食差不多。这就是对照组。然后他们观察了这些猕猴五年后的结果。结果显示，那些限制了热量摄入、少吃30%热量的猴子，比对照组寿命延长了26%。

cues.en: 50% less cardiovascular disease and greater than 90% no diabetes. Just by cutting calories down. Our food is so full of calories. The more calories you eat, the more disease you're going to get. There's absolutely no doubt. So now, the NIH, they didn't want to be outdone, so they did a study. They also did 30% caloric restriction.
cues.zh: 心血管疾病减少了50%，超过90%的人没有患上糖尿病。仅仅是通过减少热量摄入。我们的食物热量太高了。你吃进去的热量越多，患病的几率就越高。这是毫无疑问的。所以现在，NIH也不甘示弱，他们也做了一项研究。他们同样实施了30%的热量限制。

cues.en: But in the control group, now watch what they did in the control group, they gave them plant proteins, no animal protein except for a little bit of fish, 5% fat only, so they gave them some fat, 4% sugar in their diet, and they were only fed twice a day. And what did they find? What do you think? Did those monkeys do better than the 30% caloric restriction, or do you think it was as good as the caloric restriction?
cues.zh: 但在对照组中，注意看他们对对照组做了什么，给它们喂的是植物蛋白，除了少许鱼肉外没有动物蛋白，只有5%的脂肪，也就是给它们补充了些脂肪，饮食中含糖量为4%，而且每天只喂两次。结果他们发现了什么？你们觉得呢？是这些猴子的表现比那组限制30%热量的更好，还是说效果和限制热量一样好？

cues.en: They did better. So again, it's your diet. So just simply cutting down on 30% calories is not the way to go. It's no longer calories in, calories out. It's how your body reacts to the calories and what calories go in. It's your hormonal response, how you respond hormonally and how you respond through your genetic expression. So be careful what goes past the tongue.
cues.zh: 它们的表现甚至更好。所以说到底，还是饮食结构的问题。因此，单纯减少30%的热量并不是长久之计。这已经不再是“摄入热量与消耗热量”那么简单了。关键在于你的身体对这些热量如何反应，以及你摄入的是什么样的热量。这取决于你的激素反应，你的激素如何应对，以及你的基因表达如何响应。所以，吃下肚的每一口都要留心。

cues.en: because that's going to determine your future. And you know, I always like questions and answers, so I'm going to stop right there. But today's main message is if you want to do a serious fast, talk to somebody who knows a lot about fasting, do it with somebody, talk to your doctor if you're on diabetes medications or blood pressure medications. If you want to simply replicate the Paleolithic way,
cues.zh: 因为这将决定你的未来。你们知道的，我一直很喜欢问答环节，所以我就讲到这里。不过今天的核心信息是，如果你想进行一次严格的断食，一定要去咨询精通断食的人，找个人一起做，如果你在吃糖尿病药或降压药，务必先咨询你的医生。如果你只是想模仿旧石器时代的生活方式，

cues.en: eat once a day or twice a day only, do it in a time-restricted fashion, all of you can do it. All of you. You don't need medical permission to do that. The only time I'm telling you to seek more help is if you want a three-day, five-day, or seven-day water fast, or even more water fast, all right? And there's a lot of books that you all can read, especially Jason Fung's book.
cues.zh: 每天只吃一顿或两顿，在限定的时间窗口内进食，你们所有人都能做到。所有人。这并不需要医生的许可。我唯一建议你去寻求专业帮助的情况，是你想进行三天、五天、七天甚至更长时间的清水断食，明白了吗？这方面有很多书大家可以去读，尤其是 Jason Fung 的书。

cues.en: And if there are any other questions, by the way, as I said before, this talk, I'll put my slides in there and then post it onto YouTube. Galen Foundation wants to continue doing stuff like this. So my next one, I want to talk about all sorts of things, including sleep. I'm going to do a whole topic on sleep and how to improve your sleep. That's so important. So I want to do that. But, you know, Galen needs help, as usual.
cues.zh: 如果大家还有其他问题，顺便说一下，正如我之前提到的，这次演讲我会把幻灯片放进去，然后上传到 YouTube。Galen Foundation 想继续办这类活动。所以我的下一场演讲，想聊聊各种各样的话题，包括睡眠。我会专门做一个关于睡眠以及如何改善睡眠的专题。这非常重要。所以我想做这个。不过，你们也知道，Galen 和往常一样需要支持。

cues.en: So any help you all can give Galen Foundation. It's a 5013C. And if you know people who would like to help this type of organization, ask them to help us out as well. And of course, they can come to our talks and our websites as well.
cues.zh: 因此，大家能给 Galen Foundation 的任何帮助我们都感激不尽。它是一家 5013C 非营利机构。如果你认识有人愿意资助这类机构，也请让他们来支持我们。当然，他们也可以来参加我们的讲座、访问我们的网站。
